title: Writing an essay
subtitle: point of view, on the other hand, in general, consequently
summary: Use the standard essay phrases to give an opinion, show both sides, compare, generalise and explain results.

lesson.heading: What a discursive essay does
lesson.text: A **discursive essay** discusses a subject. You express your own **point of view** (= opinion), and you also show that you understand both sides of the **argument** - the reasons for something and the reasons against it.

examples.text: An **argument** is a reason to think that something is true.
Link words such as *in addition* and *however* hold the essay together.

lesson.heading: Expressing a point of view
lesson.text: You can be personal (**I believe that ...**, **It seems to me that ...**) or less personal and less direct (**Some people believe ...**, **There is an argument that ...**). In written essays it is usually better not to write *In my opinion*.

examples.text: **I believe that** people who drink and drive should go to prison.
**It seems to me that** there is a problem.
**Some people believe** that no one should be sent to prison under the age of 18.
**There is an argument that** everyone should have a university education.

lesson.heading: Giving both sides
lesson.text: To show the good side and the bad side, use **one of the advantages ... However, ...** or the pair **on the one hand ... on the other (hand) ...**.

examples.text: **One of the advantages of** being an only child is that you have more attention from your parents. **However**, it can be lonely.
**On the one hand**, computers can do many things faster than human beings. **On the other hand**, some people are becoming dependent on them.

lesson.note: We say on the other hand, not ~~on the other side~~.

lesson.heading: Comparing and contrasting
lesson.text: **Contrasting** means saying how two things are similar and how they are different. Compare groups of people, or the past and the present.

examples.text: **Compared with** my grandparents, I have had much more opportunity to travel abroad.
**In the past** people didn't have computers, but **nowadays** there is one in almost every home.
Most of the developed world has become richer. **In contrast**, many countries in Africa have become poorer.

lesson.heading: Making generalisations
lesson.text: A **generalisation** says that something is true most of the time, but not always. Instead of 'Young people prefer American films', soften it with **in general**, **on the whole** or **tend to**.

examples.text: **In general**, Japanese society is more focused on groups than individuals.
Teenagers **tend to have** more freedom than in the past.
Time **tends to go** faster as you get older.

lesson.heading: Cause and effect
rows: Poor diet is one of the main **causes** of obesity.
Obesity is often **the result of** a bad diet.
They don't exercise, and **consequently** they put on weight.
Pollution can have an **effect on** people's breathing.
lesson.note: **Consequently** means the same as *as a result*.

lesson.text: Affect is the verb, effect is the noun: smoking affects your health / smoking has an effect on your health.

exercises.prompt: Match each essay skill with an example sentence.

pairs.right: Some people believe we should never go to war.
Canada has a smaller population than the USA.
Animals die because we're cutting down the forest.
TV can make children lazy. However, some programmes are educational.
People tend to retire at a later age.

exercises.prompt: One word is missing: 'It seems ___ me that there is a problem.'
exercises.explanation: It seems to me that ... expresses a personal point of view.

exercises.prompt: One word is missing: 'One of the advantages ___ studying law is that it should lead to a good career.'
exercises.explanation: One of the advantages of + noun or -ing.

exercises.prompt: One word is missing: 'It is important to give ___ sides of the argument.'
exercises.explanation: A discursive essay gives both sides of the argument.

exercises.prompt: One word is missing: 'Too much television can have a bad effect ___ children.'
exercises.explanation: Have an effect on someone. Effect is a noun.

exercises.prompt: One word is missing: 'People like freedom of choice. On the other ___, too much choice can be a bad thing.'
exercises.explanation: The phrase is on the other hand, not on the other side.

exercises.prompt: One word is missing: 'Time tends ___ go faster as you get older.'
exercises.explanation: Tend to + verb = usually do something.

exercises.prompt: Advertising is so powerful that it ___ people to buy things they don't want.
exercises.explanation: Cause someone to do something. Affect cannot be followed by to + verb.

exercises.prompt: There is not enough food, and ___ people are dying.
exercises.explanation: Consequently = as a result of this.

exercises.prompt: Essay: 'One of the advantages of the Internet is that children have access to so much information. ___, they can do this from their own homes.'
exercises.explanation: In addition adds a second advantage.

exercises.prompt: Essay: '___, some of the information on the Internet is unreliable and out of date.'
exercises.explanation: However introduces the disadvantage after the advantages.

exercises.prompt: Essay: 'If we don't control this, the Internet could have a bad ___ on children.'
exercises.explanation: Effect is the noun: have an effect on someone.

exercises.prompt: Make this a comparison between the past and the present.
words: they spend most of their time
exercises.answer: In the past children played on their bikes, but nowadays they spend most of their time in front of a computer
exercises.explanation: In the past ... but nowadays ... compares then and now.
It is a simple statement. To generalise, write: In general people are conservative, or People tend to be conservative.
